subject: Cybersecurity
title: The Yahoo Breach Lawsuits: Setting the Standard for Negligence
description: A quick win: understand The Yahoo Breach Lawsuits: Setting the Standard for Negligence.

hook.text: Yahoo was breached in 2013 and 2014, exposing all 3 billion user accounts. They hid it until 2016, during a sale to Verizon.

buildup.text: The breach cut Yahoo’s sale price by $350 million. Lawsuits alleged Yahoo failed to implement basic security like encryption.

discovery.text: Yahoo settled for $117.5 million – the largest data breach settlement at the time – setting standards for corporate liability.

twist.text: Yahoo’s CISO had requested security upgrades for years. Management rejected them as too expensive. It cost them billions.

climax.text: The Yahoo case proved that companies face real financial consequences for security negligence – changing boardroom priorities.

punchline.text: They saved on security. It cost them $350 million.

quiz.question: What impact did the Yahoo breach have on the company's sale?
options: It reduced the sale price by $350 million and led to a $117.5M settlement
